sections.h: The Shepherd of Hermas: the tower built on the rock (Similitude 9)
sections.b: The Shepherd of Hermas, a Roman Christian work that Kirsopp Lake dates to about AD 148, tells the church as a tower twice. In Similitude 9 the tower rises on a white rock with a gate cut in it, both "the Son of God" (Shepherd of Hermas 89:1). Angels build it; twelve virgins carry each stone through the gate, and only stones they carry turn white; a tall "glorious man," the Son, tests every stone and rejects the rotten ones, which the angel of repentance reworks (Shepherd of Hermas 83:3; Shepherd of Hermas 84:2). The tower, the Shepherd says, is the church (Shepherd of Hermas 90:1). The finished tower looks like one stone with the rock, because believers become "one spirit, one body" (Shepherd of Hermas 90:5, echoing Ephesians 4:4). The building pauses so that the fallen may repent and return (Shepherd of Hermas 91:2). The picture develops 1 Peter 2:5 and Ephesians 2:20-22.
sections.refs: Shepherd of Hermas 89:1; Shepherd of Hermas 90:1-5; Shepherd of Hermas 91:2; Ephesians 2:20-22; Ephesians 4:4; 1 Peter 2:5

common: Early Christians pictured the church as a building of living stones resting on Christ (1 Peter 2:5; Ephesians 2:20-22); the Shepherd of Hermas tells it as a tower on a rock that is the Son of God.

sections.h: The Shepherd of Hermas: rock, gate and glorious man
sections.b: In Similitude 9 of the Shepherd of Hermas the rock and the gate "are the Son of God" (Shepherd of Hermas 89:1). The rock is old because "The Son of God is older than all his creation. So he became the Father's counselor for his creation" (Shepherd of Hermas 89:2); the gate is new "because he appeared in the last days, at the completion of the age" (Shepherd of Hermas 89:3), and it is the only way into the kingdom. His name "cannot be contained, and it holds up the whole world" (Shepherd of Hermas 91:5). J. B. Lightfoot cited these lines to show that Hermas was no Ebionite. Yet the same book says "that Spirit is the Son of God" (Shepherd of Hermas 78:1) and pictures the Son as a "glorious man" among six angels (Shepherd of Hermas 89:8), so that Lake judged its Christology "very hard to reconstruct."
sections.refs: Shepherd of Hermas 78:1; Shepherd of Hermas 89:1-8; Shepherd of Hermas 91:5; Colossians 1:15-17; Hebrews 1:3; Hebrews 9:26

uncommon: Some readers have taken the Shepherd of Hermas to identify the Son of God with the Holy Spirit (Shepherd of Hermas 78:1), a view John Chapman (1910) reports as held "with some reason" while judging Hermas's words unclear.

sections.h: The Shepherd of Hermas: angels who build the church
sections.b: In the Shepherd of Hermas the crowd that builds the tower are "glorious angels," a wall around the Lord, and six glorious angels walk at the right and left of the Son of God, who is taller than the tower (Shepherd of Hermas 89:6-8). None of them "will come in to God without him." The angel of repentance, the Shepherd himself, was "given" to Hermas by "the glorious angel" (Shepherd of Hermas 78:3) and is entrusted with the rejected stones (Shepherd of Hermas 84:1-2). Hermas does not say whether his "glorious angel" and "glorious man" are one figure. In Similitude 8 the glorious angel is Michael (Shepherd of Hermas 69:3), and Kirsopp Lake's footnote there adds, "But in Sim. ix. he is the Son of God."
sections.refs: Shepherd of Hermas 78:3; Shepherd of Hermas 84:1-2; Shepherd of Hermas 89:6-8; Shepherd of Hermas 69:3; Hebrews 1:4-6; Revelation 21:12

sections.h: Numbers in the Shepherd of Hermas: twelve and the four foundation rows
sections.b: Similitude 9 of the Shepherd of Hermas is built on twelves: twelve mountains, explained as twelve tribes living in the whole world (Shepherd of Hermas 94:1), twelve virgins (virtues) and twelve women in black (vices), each group with four stronger members (Shepherd of Hermas 92:2-3). The foundation is four rows of stones from the deep, ten, twenty (or twenty-five), thirty-five and forty: the first generation, the second generation of the righteous, the prophets and God's servants, and the apostles and teachers (Shepherd of Hermas 92:4). The witnesses disagree on the second number, and Kirsopp Lake wrote that "no satisfactory hypothesis has ever been suggested as to any hidden meaning which the numbers may conceal."
sections.refs: Shepherd of Hermas 78:4; Shepherd of Hermas 81:3; Shepherd of Hermas 82:4; Shepherd of Hermas 92:2-4; Shepherd of Hermas 94:1; Revelation 21:12-14

sections.h: The Shepherd of Hermas: twelve virgins who are virtues
sections.b: The Shepherd of Hermas pictures the virtues as twelve virgins who carry believers into the church (Shepherd of Hermas 79:3; Shepherd of Hermas 81:8). They are "holy spirits" and "powers of the Son of God" (Shepherd of Hermas 90:2), and their names are Faith, Self-control, Power, Patience, Simplicity, Innocence, Purity, Cheerfulness, Truth, Discernment, Harmony and Love (Shepherd of Hermas 92:2). Four of them are in Paul's list of the Spirit's fruit: love, patience, faithfulness, self-control (Galatians 5:22-23). Bearing the name of the Son without wearing these virtues "will do you no good at all" (Shepherd of Hermas 90:2), and their opposites are twelve women in black, led by Unbelief and Lack of Self-control (Shepherd of Hermas 92:3).
sections.refs: Shepherd of Hermas 90:2-5; Shepherd of Hermas 92:2-3; Galatians 5:22-23; 2 Peter 1:5-7; Colossians 3:12-14

sections.h: The Shepherd of Hermas: the rock and gate, and rejected stones
sections.b: The Shepherd of Hermas does not use the word cornerstone, but its tower rests on a rock with a gate cut into it, and "the rock and the gate were holding up the whole tower" (Shepherd of Hermas 81:2). Both are the Son of God (Shepherd of Hermas 89:1), who "became their foundation" (Shepherd of Hermas 91:6), as in 1 Corinthians 3:11. Hermas uses the verb of Psalm 118:22 and 1 Peter 2:7, "rejected," not of Christ but of believers thrown out of the building, and most of them can still be cut and set back in (Shepherd of Hermas 84:4).
sections.refs: Shepherd of Hermas 81:2; Shepherd of Hermas 84:4; Shepherd of Hermas 89:1; Shepherd of Hermas 91:6; Psalm 118:22; 1 Peter 2:4-7; 1 Corinthians 3:11

sections.h: The Shepherd of Hermas: "that Spirit is the Son of God"
sections.b: The Shepherd of Hermas says the Holy Spirit spoke to Hermas "in the form of the Church," and adds, "For that Spirit is the Son of God" (Shepherd of Hermas 78:1). In the same parable twelve "holy spirits," the virgins, are "powers of the Son of God" who clothe believers (Shepherd of Hermas 90:2). John Chapman (Catholic Encyclopedia, 1910) reports that Hermas has been thought, "with some reason," not to distinguish the Son from the Holy Spirit, but judges his words "not clear."
sections.refs: Shepherd of Hermas 78:1-2; Shepherd of Hermas 90:2; Shepherd of Hermas 59:5; 2 Corinthians 3:17

sections.h: The Shepherd of Hermas: the pause in the building
sections.b: In Similitude 9 of the Shepherd of Hermas the tower's building stops before it is finished, and the Shepherd explains: "That is the very reason the building had a pause: so that if these people repent, they may go into the building of the tower" (Shepherd of Hermas 91:2). The rejected stones are handed to the angel of repentance to be cleaned and cut (Shepherd of Hermas 84:1-5). Even believers who had received the name and the virtues and then fell can return, but once the tower is complete those who have not repented "will be thrown out for good."
sections.refs: Shepherd of Hermas 82:1; Shepherd of Hermas 84:1-5; Shepherd of Hermas 91:1-3; Shepherd of Hermas 31:6; Hebrews 6:4-6; 2 Peter 3:9

sections.h: The Shepherd of Hermas: one gate into the kingdom
sections.b: The Shepherd of Hermas speaks of entering the kingdom of God through one gate, the Son of God: "you cannot go into the city except through the gate it has. In the same way, a person cannot enter the kingdom of God any other way except through the name of his Son" (Shepherd of Hermas 89:5). Bearing the virtues as well as the name, one "will be able to enter the kingdom of God" (Shepherd of Hermas 92:2); a slave of God who bears the vices "will see the kingdom of God, but he will not enter it" (Shepherd of Hermas 92:3), like Moses at Deuteronomy 34:4.
sections.refs: Shepherd of Hermas 89:3-5; Shepherd of Hermas 92:2-3; John 3:5; Matthew 7:13-14; Deuteronomy 34:4
